newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: LME pins alloy contract hopes on auto industry.
newsitem.headline: LME pins alloy contract hopes on auto industry.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange wants to encourage car manufacturers to price scrap metal against its struggling Aluminium Alloy Contract in order to boost liquidity and attract new customers, the LME's head of marketing said.

"(Auto manufacturers) need to be persuaded not only to buy basis LME but also to sell their scrap back to the industry basis LME," Raymond Sampson told a conference organised by the Organisation of European Aluminium Refiners and Smelters.
"That way the rest of the market can use LME pricing and so hedge successfully. This would give liquidity to the market so that the large users could then be accommodated," he continued.
Since its launch in 1992 the alloy contract has struggled to win acceptance in the face of industry scepticism.
Sampson said he hoped car manufacturers, whose off-cuts account for around 60 percent of all alloy scrap, would set an example to other potential customers and draw in market makers.

"A market that does not trade sufficiently to enable buyers, sellers and hedgers to operate with reasonable assurance that their orders will be executed at prices close to current values, cannot be used satisfactorily for price reference or hedging purposes," he said.

"The LME can do so much in promoting a contract but ultimately it is up to the industry and the trading companies to use the contract and so make the contract usable." he concluded. --Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom +43-1 531 12 254
